task.title: Make build-heavy script tests cache-aware and -short-gated
task.description:
go test ./... is unsafe to run concurrently (and slow to run at all) because the release/install script tests each build with a fresh empty GOCACHE, forcing complete cold recompiles of the entire dependency graph including the standard library, across 4 cross-compile platforms. One full suite run costs ~22 cold whole-universe builds; parallel agent fleets drove load to 95 on 18 cores twice on 2026-08-08.

Fix:
1. Use the ambient GOCACHE everywhere except TestReleaseScriptProducesDeterministicArtifacts, whose two disjoint empty caches are load-bearing (a shared cache would make the second build trivially byte-identical via cache hits).
2. Gate every test that shells out to a real 'go build' of the CLI behind testing.Short(), so 'go test -short ./...' is the safe default for local iteration and agent fleets; CI and release gates run the full suite.
3. install_default_test.go's buildEnvironment pins GOPATH/GOMODCACHE from the real environment because the test moves HOME; pin GOCACHE the same way instead of using an empty temp dir.
4. Document the -short convention in AGENTS.md testing expectations.

Follow-up candidates deliberately out of scope: merging the two archive tests (the determinism test's first artifact set can serve as the verification set, 15 cold builds -> 10) and stubbing the go toolchain in install-script tests that only assert shell behavior (mirroring the existing fake-gh pattern).
